title: Per-tenant micro-reservoir with bounded spillover and sequence-preserving replay for console metrics
creator: Maya Thompson
description: We need a per-tenant in-memory micro-reservoir layer in the console metrics ingest path that smooths short bursts, enforces soft per-tenant quotas, and deterministically spills excess events to an "cold" durable store for later sequence-preserving replay. This reduces tail latency from transient bursts, prevents noisy tenants from impacting global throughput, and preserves ordering guarantees required by downstream aggregators.
background: Current ingest pipeline folds bursts at the global ingress buffer and applies coarse tenant throttling which either drops events or forces synchronous backpressure on upstream services. This causes: (1) high p50/p95 for critical tenants during spikes, (2) tenant-induced head-of-line issues when a single tenant overloads a shard, and (3) manual interventions during promotions/marketing spikes. We want a controlled, observable per-tenant buffer that can spill to object storage and replay without violating ordering semantics.
goals: Introduce a lightweight per-tenant micro-reservoir that holds up to X events or Y MB per tenant
Implement deterministic spillover to S3/GCS when per-tenant reservoir exceeds soft limit
Support sequence-preserving async replay back into the normal stream with idempotent markers
Expose tenant-level metrics and alerts (reservoir occupancy, spill rate, replay lag)
Ensure no increased end-to-end error rate for non-spilled events and maintain SLOs
success_metrics: Reduce tenant-induced p95 ingest latency by >=30% during 1m bursts
Limit dropped events due to quota violations to <0.1% across tenants
Maintain <2s additional median latency for events that remain in-memory
Replay completion within SLA for spilled batches (target 99% within 10m)
design_decisions: Use a leaky-bucket style per-tenant reservoir with a small LRU to evict inactive tenants
Spill format is newline-delimited JSON with a compact header: tenant_id, shard_key, min_offset, max_offset
Use a monotonic per-tenant sequence token and per-event idempotency key to enable safe replay
Replay will be done via a dedicated replay worker pool that uses the same enrichment/checkpointing path as live events
Cold-store partitioning by tenant-date-hour to avoid hot object churn
implementation_notes: Reservoir lives in the ingest gateway process; memory cap per instance configured by runtime flag
When reservoir > soft_limit, mark tenant as "spill-eligible" and begin batching spill files every N seconds or M bytes
Spill write uses multipart upload to S3 with backoff and local retry; on persistent failure, raise alert and increment tenant failure counter
Replay workers read spill manifests, validate sequence tokens and replay into the same topic with a special header to prevent double-consumption
Add tracing span and tag "reservoir.spill" for end-to-end observability
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests for reservoir eviction, spill, and replay flows
E2E test that simulates 10K events/min for single tenant and verifies reduced p95 compared to baseline
Dashboard showing per-tenant reservoir occupancy, spill count, and replay lag
Canary rollout to 5% of production tenants with abort conditions defined (e.g., increased error-rate >0.5%)

risks: Spilled files might be produced faster than replay capacity, causing backlog and higher replay lag
Sequence tokens misuse could lead to duplicate writes downstream if idempotency keys are incorrect
Ingest gateway memory misconfiguration could cause OOM on heavy tenant churn
S3/GCS request throttling could amplify latency during massive simultaneous spills
mitigations: Backpressure signals from replay workers to slow spill rate when backlog grows
Conservative default reservoir sizes with telemetry-driven tuning
Circuit breaker on spill writer that flips a tenant to synchronous quota enforcement when object-store is unavailable
Monitor and alert on multipart upload error rate and per-bucket request rates
testing_plan: Unit tests for reservoir boundary behaviour and LRU eviction
Integration tests for spill write/read against a local S3 emulator
Chaos testing: simulate object-store failures and ensure circuit breaker path executes
Load test: per-tenant burst profile and global burst profile (k6 / custom harness)
Regression test: ensure replayed events preserve ordering relative to non-spilled events
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated rollout in canary cluster
Phase 1: enable for internal tenants only (0.5% traffic) - monitor dashboards
Phase 2: widen to 5% customers with automated abort on error budget burn
Phase 3: global rollout with migration notes for tenant-specific quotas
Post-rollout: 7-day readout and follow-up optimization spike to tune default limits
observability: Logs: structured spill events with spill_id, tenant_id, file_path, events_count
Traces: span names reservoir.add, reservoir.spill.write, reservoir.replay.process
Dashboard: per-tenant heatmap and global spill rate timeseries
